text:
sara: quick heads-up — I ran a few nsys profiles on the latest runtime build and saw a weird tail of small kernels spiking during KV cache misses. attaching notes.
ben: thanks, can you paste the nsys cmd you used? want to reproduce.
sara: sure — `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=run-kvmiss ./bin/infer --workload test_prompts`
sara: key observation: when reqs hit a cold KV slot we get ~8 tiny kernel launches that each take 40-120 us, and NVTX shows them interleaved with batching logic.
maya: are those kernels from quantized matmuls or some prefetch helper? looks like our recent kernel selector change could be to blame.
alejandro: curious — did you capture perfetto or the nvprof timeline too? a screenshot helps.
sara: uploaded a perfetto link (snippet) and a small nsight snapshot: https://perfetto.app/trace/xxxx (public snippet)
sara: NVTX names are messy in that trace — a bunch of "range" entries with no context. makes correlating to request ids hard.
kai: we discussed adding a per-request short id in NVTX ranges earlier. propose we add `nvtxName = fmt::format("req:{}:{}", req_short, label)` in request entry/exit.
ben: +1 for req_short. suggestion: use 8-char hex of request counter so strings stay short in timeline.
maya: also propose a naming convention: top-level range "req:<short>-route:<route>" then child ranges for "batch:enqueue", "batch:dispatch", "kernel:<name>". keeps timeline scannable.
sara: sample NVTX snippet I used to test:
```
// on request start
nvtxName = fmt::format("req:{}-route:{}", short_id, route);
nvtxRangePushA(nvtxName.c_str());
// later around kernel launch
nvtxRangePushA(fmt::format("{}-kernel:{}", short_id, kernel_tag).c_str());
// on request end
nvtxRangePop();
```
alejandro: watch out for string alloc overhead in hot paths. can pre-allocate a small buffer and sprintf into it instead of heap alloc.
kai: or maintain a thread-local short-id string buffer reused across pushes. avoids allocs and keeps NVTX text stable.
ben: on sampling: we should not instrument every tiny helper with NVTX; instead mark high-level spans and synthesize smaller spans from event logs for heavy sampling runs.
maya: agree. for perf runs we can enable verbose NVTX with an env var `INSTRUMENT_NVTX=1` and otherwise keep lightweight flags like `INSTRUMENT_NVTX=short`.
sara: repro steps I ran (so team can reproduce):
1) checkout branch `perf/kernel-selector-fix`
2) build with `make -j16 INSTRUMENT_NVTX=1`
3) run `nsys profile` above with the small prompt set (attached)
4) open perfetto, filter on "req:"

sara: result: the KV miss hotpath creates many tiny kernel launches from `prefetch_kernel_v2` which were previously fused in the older kernel selector. regression introduced in commit `c4d9a2`.
alejandro: I can bisect the selector change tomorrow. quick thought — maybe our kernel fusion heuristic lost a predicate when handling short-seq cases.
kai: in the meantime, we can add a short-circuit to avoid launching prefetch kernels when sequence_len < 8 — should reduce noise.
ben: also record a metric in console (per-request tiny-kernel-count) so we can evaluate in prod without full traces.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: perf/bisect-runner on branch `perf/kernel-selector-fix` at 2026-03-19T02:30Z :rocket:
sara: action items:
- alejandro: bisect selector and propose fix (ETA 24h)
- kai: add thread-local short-id buffer and low-overhead NVTX macros (ETA 48h)
- ben: add tiny-kernel-count metric and dashboard (ETA 72h)
- maya: patch quick short-seq prefetch short-circuit (ETA 24h)

maya: one more thing — let's add a doc blurb about NVTX naming conventions in the instrumentation README so new folks follow the pattern.
sara: agreed. I'll create the doc PR after we land the transient fixes. thanks all :thumbsup:
